scenario.title: Alstom Transport UK Ltd v London Underground Ltd
scenario.description: London Underground awarded contract to Bombardier for £112.1 million worth of AC traction motors and control equipment. Alstom challenged the award alleging a manifest error in applying a mandatory technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. The challenge was brought during the standstill period, triggering an automatic suspension. London Underground applied to lift the suspension under the American Cyanamid framework, arguing that damages would be adequate remedy for Alstom if it succeeded at trial and that the balance of convenience favoured proceeding with the contract.

interests: Protection of Public Funds: Significant delay costs due to automatic suspension
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Critical AC traction motors and control equipment for the London Underground network, with operational consequences if delivery is delayed or re-run
Reputation & Public Accountability: Maintain public confidence in the procurement process, particularly given the contract value (£112.1 million)
Minimising Litigation Risk: Balance disclosure to Alstom with maintaining evaluation confidentiality and integrity
goals: Maintain the integrity of the evaluation process
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We stand by our original evaluation, which was conducted fairly and in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023.
legal_basis: Regulation 32(1) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: £112.1 million contract value at risk if we fail to challenge the award
Fairness & Transparency: perceived unfairness in application of technical threshold requirement
Protection of Reputation: our credibility and win-rate targets are impacted by this dispute
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids, giving us a chance to be awarded the contract ourselves
An award of damages for any losses incurred due to London Underground's alleged manifest error
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We believe there was a manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement, which should have excluded Bombardier's bid. We request a re-evaluation of all bids to ensure fairness and transparency.

messages.message: I acknowledge Alstom's challenge and appreciate the opportunity to clarify our evaluation process. Specifically, I would like to request clarification on what Alstom considers a 'manifest error' in applying the technical threshold requirement. Could you please provide more details on this assertion? Additionally, I'd like to offer transparency by providing additional information on our evaluation criteria and methodology used for scoring Bombardier's bid.

I appreciate your willingness to provide additional information on your evaluation criteria and methodology used for scoring Bombardier's bid. However, I would like to clarify what specific aspects of our challenge you are seeking to address with this offer. Could you please specify which parts of our 'manifest error' assertion you believe can be resolved through transparency regarding the evaluation process? Additionally, I would like to request that you provide a detailed breakdown of Bombardier's bid scores for each technical threshold requirement, as mentioned in the contract documentation.

I understand that Alstom is seeking a detailed breakdown of Bombardier's bid scores for each technical threshold requirement as mentioned in the contract documentation. I am willing to provide this information, but I would like to clarify that it will be based on our evaluation criteria and methodology used for scoring. Additionally, I would like to request more specific details from Alstom regarding their assertion of a 'manifest error' in applying the technical threshold requirement.

I appreciate your willingness to provide additional information on your evaluation criteria and methodology used for scoring Bombardier's bid. However, I would like to clarify that our assertion of a 'manifest error' in applying the technical threshold requirement is based on a specific discrepancy in scoring. Specifically, we have identified a 3-point difference in scores between our bid and Bombardier's bid under the same technical threshold requirement. We believe this discrepancy is significant enough to warrant a re-evaluation of both bids. Regarding your request for more details from Alstom regarding our assertion, I am willing to provide further information on our internal evaluation process, but only if you are able to provide a detailed breakdown of Bombardier's bid scores for each technical threshold requirement as mentioned in the contract documentation.

Specifically, I would like to know what specific discrepancy in scoring they have identified and how it relates to our evaluation criteria and methodology used for scoring.

We acknowledge that the discrepancy in scoring is a critical aspect of our challenge. Specifically, we have identified a 3-point difference in scores between our bid and Bombardier's bid under the same technical threshold requirement. We believe this discrepancy is significant enough to warrant a re-evaluation of both bids. In light of your request for clarification on this point, we propose that you provide an explanation for this scoring discrepancy, including any relevant documentation or evaluation records that support the 3-point difference in scores.

I acknowledge Alstom's assertion that a 3-point difference in scores between their bid and Bombardier's bid under the same technical threshold requirement is significant enough to warrant a re-evaluation of both bids. I am willing to provide additional information on our evaluation criteria and methodology used for scoring, including any relevant documentation or evaluation records that support the scoring process. However, I would like to request that Alstom clarify how they arrived at their assertion of a 'manifest error' in applying the technical threshold requirement.

I would like to clarify that our assertion of a 'manifest error' in applying the technical threshold requirement is based on a specific discrepancy in scoring, which we believe is significant enough to warrant a re-evaluation of both bids. I propose that we narrow the disagreement by focusing on this specific issue and provide a detailed breakdown of Bombardier's bid scores for each technical threshold requirement as mentioned in the contract documentation.

I am willing to provide a detailed breakdown of Bombardier's bid scores for each technical threshold requirement as mentioned in the contract documentation, and I propose that we accept Alstom's assertion that a 3-point difference in scores between their bid and Bombardier's bid under the same technical threshold requirement is significant enough to warrant a re-evaluation of both bids. In light of this, I am willing to offer a voluntary standstill extension for engagement and further discussion on how we can proceed with a revised evaluation process.
messages.concession_made: A voluntary standstill extension for engagement

messages.message: I am willing to accept a voluntary re-evaluation of both bids, with a focus on resolving the discrepancy in scoring under the technical threshold requirement. I propose that we conduct a joint review of the evaluation process and provide a detailed breakdown of Bombardier's bid scores for each technical threshold requirement as mentioned in the contract documentation. If this process reveals a manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement, I am willing to accept a re-run of the evaluation process.
messages.proposal: A voluntary re-evaluation of both bids with a focus on resolving the discrepancy in scoring under the technical threshold requirement

However, I do not see any evidence of manifest error in applying this requirement. The parties' positions focus on transparency and clarification rather than a specific numerical calculation. Therefore, I conclude that the Contracting Authority followed a lawful process.

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The negotiation outcome is slightly favourable compared to our BATNA (defending in TCC court, which would cost £50k+ and take 6-12 months). While we did not achieve a full win, the deadlock reached after five rounds of negotiations means that we avoided the costs and risks associated with further litigation.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated a voluntary standstill extension for engagement and further discussion on how to proceed with a revised evaluation process. This outcome allows us to maintain control over the contract award process while also addressing Alstom's concerns regarding the technical threshold requirement.

summary.concessions_summary: Both parties made concessions throughout the negotiation, but ultimately reached a deadlock. The Contracting Authority offered a voluntary standstill extension for engagement and proposed a re-evaluation of both bids. Alstom accepted this proposal and suggested conducting a joint review of the evaluation process.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round qualitatively due to the technical nature of the dispute. They concluded that the Contracting Authority followed a lawful process, but did not identify any manifest error in applying the technical threshold requirement. The Court recommended continuing negotiation and encouraged both parties to engage in further discussion.
summary.likely_next_steps: The case will likely escalate to formal proceedings as the parties reached a deadlock after five rounds of negotiation. A re-evaluation of the bids may be conducted, but this is not guaranteed.
summary.plain_english_summary: The dispute centered on a scoring discrepancy between Alstom's bid and Bombardier's bid under the technical threshold requirement. Both parties made concessions, but ultimately failed to reach an agreement. The Court concluded that the Contracting Authority followed a lawful process, but did not identify any manifest error. The case will likely proceed to formal proceedings.
